facts.claim: Backend source under src/main/java/com/pubginsight/ contains feature packages player/, match/, insight/, history/, health/, common/ (config+exception) and client/ with subpackages pubg/, gemini/, s3/, dynamodb/.

PlayerController exposes GET /api/players/{name} and GET /api/players/{playerId}/season-stats; MatchController exposes GET /api/players/{playerId}/matches/{matchId}; InsightController exposes GET /api/players/{playerId}/matches/{matchId}/insights; HistoryController exposes POST and GET .../matches/{matchId}/history; HealthController exposes GET /health.

Frontend services call exactly: GET /health (App.tsx), GET /api/players/{name} and GET /api/players/{playerId}/season-stats (playerService/seasonStatsService), GET /api/players/{playerId}/matches/{matchId} (matchService), GET .../insights (insightService). No frontend service currently calls the /history endpoint - HistoryController exists in the backend but is not yet wired to any UI.
The frontend has exactly one external call surface: src/api/axios.ts, a shared axios instance with baseURL = VITE_API_BASE_URL. It never calls PUBG/Gemini/AWS directly.

Compile-time dependencies: player -> client.pubg; match -> client.pubg; match -> client.s3; insight -> player, insight -> match, insight -> client.gemini; history -> match, history -> insight, history -> client.dynamodb. common.exception depends on (catches exceptions from) player, match, client.pubg, client.gemini, client.dynamodb - the reverse of a typical dependency direction, a deliberate design choice (D1) so feature packages stay independent of each other.

PUBG Developer API and Google Gemini API are both live external integrations: PubgApiClient (rate-limited via PubgRateLimiter, sliding 60s window, blocking) and GeminiApiClient are implemented, called over real HTTPS with Bearer token / API key respectively, and verified working end-to-end against real data (Feature 1 Player Search and Feature 2 Match Analytics verified live per PROJECT_CONTEXT.md; Feature 3 AI Insights code complete).

CORRECTED 2026-09-13: client.s3 (S3MatchCacheClient, cache-aside for match JSON, soft-fail on error per D12) and client.dynamodb (AnalysisHistoryRepository, analysis-history persistence, hard-fail/502 on error per D12) are now DEPLOYED AND VERIFIED against the real personal AWS account. PROJECT_CONTEXT.md's Current Status section states: 'DynamoDB table (pubg-insight-analysis-history) and S3 bucket (pubg-insight-match-cache) created on the personal AWS account and verified working end-to-end against real AWS' - confirmed via a real GET .../matches/{id} called twice showing a visible speedup on the second call with no S3Exception warnings (cache-aside working), and a real POST .../matches/{id}/history followed by GET .../history round-tripping a real item through DynamoDB. TASK.md line 65 was updated to match: 'Create the DynamoDB table and S3 bucket - done and verified'. This supersedes an earlier reading of these same docs (pre-correction) that had said bucket/table creation was still pending - that was based on a stale doc snapshot.

CORRECTED 2026-09-14: the backend is now actually deployed and running on AWS Elastic Beanstalk - Java/Corretto 21 platform, 'Single Instance' environment tier (explicitly not Load Balanced, so there is no ALB in front of it; the single EC2 instance gets its own public endpoint). The frontend is now actually deployed as a static website directly from an S3 bucket (pubg-insight-frontend) using S3 static website hosting - there is no CloudFront distribution in front of it. This is independently corroborated by repo-backend commit 481c108 ('feat: allow S3-hosted frontend origin in CORS config', 2026-09-14, src/main/java/com/pubginsight/common/config/CorsConfig.java): the commit adds allowedOrigins entry 'http://pubg-insight-frontend.s3-website-us-east-1.amazonaws.com' alongside the local dev origin, with commit message 'Frontend will be deployed to S3 static website hosting' - confirming both the exact bucket name/region and that the endpoint is a plain S3 website endpoint (http, not https - S3 website hosting has no native TLS, another concrete sign there is no CloudFront in front of it). This supersedes the prior 'no infrastructure created yet' reading of PROJECT_CONTEXT.md/TASK.md, which was accurate as of 2026-09-13 but is now stale.

The EC2 instance Elastic Beanstalk provisions runs under the default aws-elasticbeanstalk-ec2-role instance profile. This role needed AmazonS3FullAccess and AmazonDynamoDBFullAccess (AWS-managed policies) attached manually via the IAM console so the running Spring Boot app's AWS SDK calls (S3MatchCacheClient, AnalysisHistoryRepository) can actually reach the S3 cache bucket and DynamoDB table at runtime. This is distinct from the separate pubg-insight-dev IAM user documented in AWS_SETUP.md, which is for local/developer programmatic access, not the deployed instance's runtime identity. No custom-scoped IAM policy exists - only the two AWS managed full-access policies.

API Gateway, AWS Lambda, and Amazon Athena remain genuinely not built and not deployed as of 2026-09-14, consistent with PROJECT_CONTEXT.md/TASK.md ('no code at all, no infrastructure created yet'). CloudFront, SQS, and EventBridge were never part of the approved service list and were considered and explicitly deferred. None of these six should appear in a diagram documenting the actual current deployment.

PUBG rate limiting is enforced backend-side by PubgRateLimiter (D16): a single shared component tracks a sliding 60s window of call timestamps and blocks the calling thread until a slot is free, protecting the app's one shared PUBG API key budget (10 req/min) regardless of which frontend tab/request triggered the call.

Real, official-source icons were resolved and synced into this project's asset manifest for: Amazon S3, Amazon DynamoDB, AWS Elastic Beanstalk, and AWS IAM (extracted directly from the official AWS Architecture Service Icons ZIP, bypassing a bug in nexcanvas's own --provider aws-official --source-archive filename-discovery step that could pick a __MACOSX/._ AppleDouble junk duplicate over the real SVG when both share a near-identical normalized filename); React (from Simple Icons); Spring Boot and Google Gemini and PUBG (from Simple Icons, fetched live from the jsdelivr CDN and each verified via its embedded <title> tag before syncing). All are recorded as 'Synced'/'Embedded' in assets/asset_manifest.json. The Amazon API Gateway, AWS Lambda, and Amazon Athena icons previously synced for the (now removed) planned-services zone remain on disk unused but are no longer referenced by any node - those three services are not part of the actual deployment this diagram now documents.

New feature (added since the prior diagram pass): a client.telemetry package (TelemetryClient, WeaponNameResolver, TelemetryFetchException, dto.WeaponKillCount) plus a new match.WeaponBreakdownService/WeaponBreakdownController exposing GET /api/players/{playerId}/matches/{matchId}/weapons - a telemetry-derived per-weapon kill breakdown. WeaponBreakdownService calls PubgApiClient.findMatchRawJson() directly (its own dependency on client.pubg, separate from MatchService) to locate the match's telemetry asset URL, then calls TelemetryClient to fetch and parse it. Frontend src/services/weaponService.ts already calls this endpoint. Per TelemetryClient.java's class-level comment: telemetry files are deliberately NOT routed through PubgApiClient/PubgRateLimiter - they are static assets served from a separate CDN host (telemetry-cdn.pubg.com, taken from the match response's 'asset' resource URL), fetched unauthenticated (no Authorization/Bearer header), using a plain java.net.http.HttpClient rather than the Spring RestClient the other clients use, and are not subject to the 10 req/min PubgRateLimiter budget. This is evidenced by the community pubgjava reference client (github.com/mautini/pubgjava), whose Retrofit interface tags every other endpoint method with an '@Headers("@: Auth")' marker its interceptor uses to attach the API key, except getTelemetry(String url), which carries no such marker - documented as strong secondary evidence in the code comment itself, not a live-verified call (this sandbox's outbound proxy blocks both api.pubg.com and the telemetry CDN, category 'Online and Other Games', confirmed via curl). Failure handling is asymmetric: PubgApiException/PubgRateLimitException from the findMatchRawJson() call propagate normally (same as every other PUBG-backed endpoint), but any telemetry-specific failure (missing asset URL, CDN slow/unreachable, unparseable payload) is caught inside WeaponBreakdownService and turned into an empty list, never an error - deliberately isolating this new panel from breaking the existing match page.

assumptions: The app's own custom code (feature packages health/player/match/insight/history/weapon-breakdown, and the client.pubg/client.gemini/client.s3/client.dynamodb/client.telemetry wrapper classes) is not a named product with a logo, so these remain generic labeled glyphs even though the systems they call now have real icons.

The diagram models frontend as a single Container-level node (React Frontend) rather than breaking out individual components (PlayerSearch.tsx, MatchList.tsx, etc.) - the requested viewIntent is system/component architecture for the backend; frontend internal component structure is out of scope for this diagram.

WeaponNameResolver (an internal helper of TelemetryClient that maps raw damageCauserId strings to display names via a bundled JSON dictionary) is not modeled as its own node - it has no external call surface and is an implementation detail of TelemetryClient, consistent with how other internal helper classes are not individually diagrammed.

The 2026-09-13 revision merged External APIs and AWS-live zones into one 'External Services - Live' zone and dropped a non-runtime 'future hosting' connector; that revision's build never reached a clean QA pass (diagram-qa stage recorded status 'failed', 50 errors / 13 warnings in reports/diagram_qa.json) and its 'AWS - Planned / Not Deployed' zone (Elastic Beanstalk, API Gateway, Lambda, Athena all shown as not-yet-built) is corrected by this pass - see fact-eb-frontend-s3-deployed.

This revision (2026-09-14) is a deployment-reality audit and repair, not a re-run of repository static analysis: it corrects the diagram against orchestrator-supplied ground truth about what is actually deployed on AWS right now (audit-2026-09-14), supersedes the stale 'nothing deployed yet' facts recorded 2026-09-13, removes the topology that was the largest source of the prior QA failures (the planned-services zone and its long cross-canvas connectors to API Gateway/Lambda/Athena), and re-derives layout from the semantic model rather than reusing the previous broken connector geometry.
exclusions: Frontend's newer V2-redesign components observed in the sibling repo (PerformanceRadar.tsx, PlayerIdentityCard.tsx, DeltaIndicator.tsx, PerformanceBreakdown.tsx, AiInsights.tsx, RevealOnMount.tsx, StatTile.tsx, SectionTitle.tsx) are not individually modeled - they are all still served through the same single axios call surface and same backend controllers documented above, so they don't change the architecture-level picture this diagram shows.

Sequence-level detail (request/response steps within a single feature call) is intentionally excluded - already fully documented as Mermaid sequence diagrams in docs/deliverables/ARCHITECTURE.md; this diagram's viewIntent is architecture (system context + component view), not sequence.

API Gateway, AWS Lambda, and Amazon Athena are excluded entirely (not drawn even as 'planned') per explicit instruction: this diagram documents the actual current deployment, not the approved-but-unbuilt rubric service list. CloudFront, SQS, and EventBridge are excluded for the same reason - none exist in the current deployment.
